question.worked_solution:
First, note that $x=\frac{1}{2}$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined.

To solve the equation, we first multiply both sides by the denominator $(2x-1)$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7x+4}{2x-1} & =5 \\ (2x-1)\cdot \frac{7x+4}{2x-1} & =(2x-1)\cdot 5 \\ \cancel{(2x-1)}\cdot \frac{7x+4}{\cancel{2x-1}} & =(2x-1)\cdot 5 \\ 7x+4 & =10x-5\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}7x+4 & =10x-5 \\ 7x+4+5 & =10x-5+5 \\ 7x+9 & =10x \\ 7x+9-7x & =10x-7x \\ 9 & =3x \\ \frac{9}{3} & =\frac{3x}{3} \\ 3 & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Since $x=3$ is different from $x=\frac{1}{2}$, we can accept it as a solution. Thus, the solution is $x=3.$
